values.goal: Distinguish static type relationships from runtime data validation, and design contracts that can change.
values.capstone: A mount/dispose plugin with interchangeable DOM and Canvas implementations, plus a collection of valid and rejected cases

values.title: Types and Narrowing
values.environment: The existing Frontory preview is a limited starting example, not a complete implementation of the assignment. Implement additional files and features yourself in a separate local project. Record the installed tsc version in a separate TypeScript project. Enable strict in tsconfig.json and check with tsc --noEmit, then open the runtime exercise using compiled output or a local development server. Do not assume the browser executes TS type annotations directly.
values.concepts.0.title: Static Checking
values.concepts.0.explanation: Types check relationships in code before execution. They do not automatically inspect the actual contents of external JSON.
values.concepts.1.title: Discriminated Unions
values.concepts.1.explanation: Branching on a shared tag with different values narrows objects to the fields you need. Accessing a state-specific field outside its branch causes an error.
values.outcomes.0: Check the returned strings for all four states.
values.outcomes.1: Record the compiler diagnostic for invalid access and a correction.
values.steps.0: In state.ts, prepare conditions for access to success data and the same access in idle.
values.steps.1: Create an idle·loading·success·error union and return display strings with switch.
values.steps.2: Run with access to success data and the same access in idle. Results to check: Check the returned strings for all four states. Record the compiler diagnostic for invalid access and a correction. Record expected and actual results separately.
values.variables.0.name: Access Location
values.variables.0.expected: Pre-run hypothesis: the compiler will reject unsafe access. Keep other conditions fixed and record the actual result separately after running.
values.criteria.0: Check the returned strings for all four states.
values.criteria.1: Record the compiler diagnostic for invalid access and a correction.
values.questions.0: Does passing type checking mean that input has been validated?
values.questions.1: How does a union differ from an object with only optional fields?
values.references.0.title: TypeScript Handbook
values.references.1.title: TypeScript Narrowing

values.concepts.0.title: Array Elements
values.concepts.0.explanation: An array type defines a common contract for all elements. Index access does not guarantee that the index is in bounds.
values.concepts.1.title: Tuples
values.concepts.1.explanation: A tuple expresses types by position and relationships involving length. It suits small data structures where order matters, such as coordinates.

values.concepts.0.title: Function Types
values.concepts.0.explanation: Parameters and return types express a call contract. An explicit return type makes missing return paths easier to find.
